description: The AI4RA UDM glossary. Edit this file, then run scripts/generate_glossary.py. Each term may list udm references (Table, Table.Column, or Table.Column=Value), which scripts/check_glossary.py validates against udm_schema.json, and a source for facts taken from a published rule.

terms.definition: A submission status: the sponsor took the proposal in for consideration. This doesn't promise a review or an award, and the sponsor can still return it. This starts the sponsor decision stage.
The full set of codes (fund, organization, account, program, or equivalent) that tells the accounting system where a charge goes.
How long invoices sent to sponsors have gone unpaid, counted from the date each was sent.
An award status: the award is open for spending within its period of performance.
A subaward status: the agreement is executed and open for the subrecipient's work.
Awards currently open for work and spending.
An award status: the award has ended and a late correction is under way, such as an audit finding or a late charge. It is not open for spending. It returns to the status it came from.
A subaward status: the subaward has ended and a late correction is under way. It is not open for work or spending. It returns to the status it came from.
The unit that manages the finances of a proposal, award, or subaward.
The institution's approval to spend on an existing award ahead of a sponsor amendment. The institution carries the risk until the amendment arrives.
The sponsor pays before the costs are incurred. This is a way of being paid, not an approval to spend.
A harmful or unexpected event on an approved protocol.

terms.also: Controlled vocabulary, code list, picklist, lookup values
terms.definition: The agreed list of codes that can be used for a field, such as the list of proposal types.

terms.also: Total anticipated funding, total award value
terms.definition: The total an award is expected to receive over its whole life if every planned increment is funded.
Original investigation done to gain new knowledge, directed mainly toward a specific, practical aim or objective.
The gate that decides whether the content of the proposal is approved. It is tracked in internal approval.
One decision in an approval chain: who was asked to decide what, and what they decided.
An early setup status: at-risk spending is authorized up to the maximum amount within the effective window.
An internal approval status: every approval step on the material has approved. Sign-off to submit is separate.
A modification status: the sponsor or institution approved the modification. It counts in the award's current totals and dates from approval, and Effective_Date records when the change takes effect.
The number that identifies a federal funding program.
One transmission of a package to a sponsor. A proposal can have several attempts, and earlier attempts stay as history.
The person who can legally commit the institution to a proposal or agreement.

The money still free to commit on an award: its funding minus money spent and money set aside for future expenses. It is the institution's counterpart to the unobligated balance. See Spending for what counts as money spent.
The money spent on an award divided by the months passed in its period. See Spending for what counts as money spent.
Funding the institution has received for a project.

The money sponsors obligated in a period: funding on new awards plus funding added to existing awards, minus funding taken back. Planned future increments don't count until they are obligated. This follows how federal spending data counts obligations.
The number the sponsor assigns to an award.
The share of applications that are funded, following NIH's method, with each resubmission counted separately. It is usually lower than the success rate because the bottom number is larger.
Where an award stands: in setup, active, suspended, closing, closed, adjusting, terminating, or terminated.
A decision status: the sponsor funded the proposal, and an Award record exists.

terms.also: Award amount, obligated amount, funded amount
terms.definition: The money the sponsor has actually committed to an award so far.
Experimental or theoretical work done mainly to gain new knowledge of the foundations of phenomena and observable facts, with no particular application or use in view.
A structured summary of a researcher's education, positions, and contributions, required in many federal proposals.
An action status: the task is waiting on something outside the assignee's control.
A general announcement, common with defense agencies, inviting proposals in broad research areas, often leading to contracts.
The planned and actual money for a proposal, award, or subaward, by line item and period.
A heading in a budget, such as salaries, fringe, equipment, travel, participant support, or other direct costs.
A slice of the period of performance for which money is budgeted and released.
Any change to an award's approved budget. A rebudget is one kind.

The share of an award's budget that has been spent, divided by the share of its period that has passed. Above 1, or 100%, means spending is ahead of time. Sponsors don't define a standard formula, so this follows common sponsored programs usage. Spending counts as on the federal financial report, without open purchase orders or cost share. See Spending for what counts as money spent.
A plain-language explanation of what a data element means, in the terms people who use it would use.
An ID used for organizations doing business with the U.S. government, especially defense.
An action status: the task was stopped before it finished and won't be completed.
A payment status: no payment will occur.

Payments for movable equipment above the institution's capitalization threshold, including delivery and setup, as the HERD survey counts them. Check the institution's capitalization policy for its threshold.
Moving unspent money from one budget period into the next. No new money comes from the sponsor.
Automating the build, test, and release of software each time a change is committed.

terms.also: Research area, subject tag, keyword, science code
terms.definition: A subject or research-area tag on a proposal, award, subaward, or compliance requirement.
A payment status: nothing is wrong with the payment.
An award status: closeout is complete.
A subaward status: closeout is complete.
The process of formally ending an award or subaward.
An award status: the period of performance has ended, and closeout is under way.
A subaward status: the period of performance has ended, and closeout is under way, including the final invoice.
The Defense Department's cybersecurity assessment program, required for some defense contracts and subcontracts. Check the Defense Department for current levels and requirements.
A senior researcher who contributes substantially to a project but does not lead it.
A person who shares leadership of a project with the PI.
The federal agency that reviews and negotiates an institution's indirect cost rates on behalf of federal agencies. The agency overseeing its audits may be a different one.
The same comparison as burn rate, with money set aside for future expenses counted along with money spent. See Spending for what counts as money spent.
The share of time promised to a project in the proposal or award.
A body that meets and decides, such as an IRB, IACUC, IBC, conflict-of-interest committee, research security board, or internal funding panel.
A message between the institution and an outside party.
An award won through competition, whether a new award or a renewal. New awards and renewals are counted separately, and this is the two added together where both were competed.
An action status: the task achieved its outcome.
A regulatory approval a project needs, such as IRB, IACUC, IBC, conflict of interest, radiation safety, or export control.

An outside relationship (financial, consulting, employment, equity, royalty, board) that could affect a person's research. People disclose these relationships, and the institution reviews whether each one is a conflict.
On a multiple-PI award, the one PI the sponsor treats as its main contact.
Funding for a later period of an existing award without a new competition.
A periodic re-review of an approved protocol. Whether and how often it is needed depends on the governing rule.
A legally binding agreement in which the sponsor buys specific work or deliverables, usually with stricter terms.
The sponsor official with legal authority to sign and change a contract.
Government information that is not classified but must be protected.
An early setup status: the award arrived, and the at-risk spending folds into the executed funding.
Funding in which the sponsor is substantially involved in doing the work alongside the institution.

terms.also: Cost sharing, matching or match (required cost share)
terms.definition: The part of project costs paid by the institution or a third party rather than the sponsor.
Moving a charge from one award or account to another after it was first posted.
A fact about a person the institution needs on file: citizenship or visa status, sponsor-system login, completed training, clearance, background check, or a standing authority.
A field-by-field mapping from a source system to the UDM, including value translations and notes on any changes. In a medallion lakehouse, it lives in the Silver layer.
An inventory of an organization's data assets: what exists, where it lives, who owns it, how it is refreshed, and who may use it.
The role responsible for operating a dataset: storage, backups, access, security, and availability. Custodians carry out what the owner decides.
A description of the data in a system: what each field means, why it exists, its type, its constraints, and how it connects to other data.
How recent the data on a report is.
The policies, standards, and procedures that keep an organization's data accurate, secure, and available, including who owns it and how decisions about it are made.
A large storage area that holds raw data from many systems in its original form, to be organized later.
A combination of a data lake and a data warehouse: raw data is kept cheaply, then refined in stages into reliable tables.
Where a number on a report came from and how it was calculated.

terms.also: DMP, data management and sharing plan, DMSP
terms.definition: A proposal document describing what data a project will produce, and how it will be stored, protected, and shared.
A shared description of what information an organization keeps: the things it tracks, the details recorded about each, and how they connect.
The person, role, or team accountable for a dataset: who fixes problems, answers questions about its meaning, and approves changes.
A dataset isolated in one system, team, or department, so that it is hard to query from anywhere else.
The kind of value a column holds, such as text, number, date, or true/false. It limits what can be stored and what can be done with it.
A central database built for reporting, pulling cleaned data together from many systems.
A one-off future obligation attached to a record, for a date with no home of its own. Due dates that belong to a report, action, or funding announcement stay on those records.
The outcome of the funding request: unrequested, pending, intent to award, awarded, declined, not reviewed, or withdrawn.
A decision status: the sponsor reviewed the proposal and did not fund it.
Money spent on an award beyond its funding, so its unspent balance is below zero. See Spending for what counts as money spent.
A value worked out from other records rather than typed in, such as an award's current end date.
Costs that can be tied to a specific project, such as salaries, supplies, and travel.
A payment status: the payer or payee contests the payment.
A file attached to any record, kept with its versions.
An internal approval status: the proposal is being prepared and has not been routed for approval.
A deliverable status: the project team is preparing it.
The older Dun and Bradstreet organization number once used for federal awards.

Recovered indirect costs as a percentage of direct costs. It is usually well below the negotiated rate because some costs carry no indirect costs and some sponsors pay less than that rate. Sponsors don't define a standard formula, so this follows common university usage.

terms.also: Time and effort, level of effort
terms.definition: The portion of a person's work time spent on a project, expressed as a percentage or in person-months.

terms.also: Effort reporting, time and effort certification
terms.definition: A person's after-the-fact confirmation that the effort charged to their projects reasonably reflects the work done.
An organization's federal tax ID number.
In institutional accounting, money set aside for a future expense, such as an open purchase order or future salary.
A major item bought for a project that meets a cost and useful-life threshold. Check 2 CFR 200.1 and the institution's capitalization policy for current thresholds.
Deciding what happens to equipment at the end of an award.
NIH's online system where applicants, recipients, and federal staff handle grant administration.

terms.also: Electronic research administration system, grants management system, ERA
terms.definition: Software for managing research funding: proposals, routing and approvals, awards, and often compliance.
Pipeline code that extracts data from a source, transforms it according to the crosswalk, and loads it into the target.
Systematic work, drawing on research and practical experience and producing additional knowledge, directed at producing new products or processes or improving existing ones.
An early setup status: the window closed without an award and without conversion.
Federal rules on sharing certain technology, items, and information with foreign persons or countries.
R&D expenditures from every source except institutional funds, as the HERD survey counts them.
The percentage applied to a cost base to calculate indirect costs.
A submission status: the attempt did not reach the sponsor's system, so the same package can be resent. Its sign-off stands.
The unique number a federal agency gives a financial assistance award.
The standard federal form reporting how award money was spent.
Whether federal rules govern an award, either because the sponsor is federal or because federal money reaches it through another organization.
The research discipline that R&D spending is reported under, from the HERD survey's list of fields. A project spanning several fields is prorated where possible.

terms.also: ERP, general ledger, accounting system, ERP system
terms.definition: The institution's accounting software, where money is officially recorded: budgets, charges, payments, and account codes.
The institution's yearly accounting period.
A column whose value must match a primary key in another table. The referenced table is the parent, and the table holding the column is the child.
The cost of employee benefits charged along with salaries, usually as a percentage rate.
A deliverable status: the sponsor reviewed and approved the deliverable, and the obligation is met.
A code in the accounting system that tracks a pool of money.

terms.also: Activity code, award type, grant type
terms.definition: The kind of funding vehicle, such as a research grant, training grant, cooperative agreement, or contract.

terms.also: RFA, FOA, NOFO, solicitation, program announcement
terms.definition: A sponsor's announcement inviting proposals, with its rules, deadlines, and funding limits.

The share of new, competitively reviewed proposals with a final decision that were awarded, counting awards and declines, following NSF's method. NSF sometimes calls this a success rate, but it is not NIH's success rate.
A list of terms and what they mean. A data dictionary applies those terms to a specific dataset, and a catalog indexes all the datasets.
Money given to carry out a project, with the sponsor having limited involvement in the work.
The sponsor's contact for the business and financial side of an award.
The federal website for finding and applying to federal grant opportunities.

terms.also: Higher Education Research and Development Survey
terms.definition: The NSF survey of university research spending.
The institution's personnel system, which holds appointments, salaries, and employee records.

terms.also: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee
terms.definition: The committee that reviews and approves research involving vertebrate animals.
The committee that reviews research with recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecules, and often other biological hazards under institutional policy.

A modification that is Approved or Not_Required and whose Effective_Date has arrived. Is_In_Effect records this. An award's current totals and dates count every approved modification from approval, even before its effective date.
An action status: the task is being worked on.
An internal approval status: the proposal has been routed, and one or more approval steps are open.
An award status: the award has been received and is in setup, and it is not yet open for spending. Review, negotiation, and account setup can all happen here.
A subaward status: the prime award exists, and the subaward agreement is being issued.
Goods, services, or donated time contributed instead of cash.
An additional installment of money added to an existing award. The installment was already planned, and the work doesn't change.

terms.also: F&A, facilities and administrative costs, overhead, IDC
terms.definition: Shared institutional costs that support research but cannot be tied to one project, such as buildings, utilities, libraries, and administration.

R&D money from the institution itself, as the HERD survey counts it: institutionally financed research, committed cost sharing, and unrecovered indirect costs. Research administration and support, such as the sponsored programs office, is not institutionally financed research.
A decision status: the sponsor has signaled funding, but no agreement exists yet.
The approvals of a proposal's material inside the institution. Sign-off to submit is a separate gate.
The institution's own ID for an award in its financial or research systems.
The person the institution holds accountable as principal investigator, under its own PI eligibility policy.
A submission status: the sponsor's system received the attempt and rejected it on its checks. The package must be fixed and signed off again. Material approval stands.
A report to the sponsor listing inventions made under the award, or stating there were none.

terms.also: Credit split, credit allocation, research credit
terms.definition: How credit for an award is divided among investigators and their units.
A request for payment sent to a sponsor, or received from a subrecipient.
A payment stage: the payment has been billed, and it carries an invoice number.
The committee that reviews and approves research involving human participants.

Information a sponsor (especially NIH) asks for after review, while an application is under consideration, such as other support, compliance approvals, and training. A request does not mean an award will follow.
People the sponsor considers essential to the project, often named in the award. Changing them may need sponsor approval.
A deliverable status: it is past its due date and has not been submitted.
A federal arrangement that lets an institution draw funds as it needs them. Check the sponsor for its current payment system.
One of the steps a record moves through, such as a budget going from proposed to approved to current to actual. Each step is kept so earlier stages remain as history.
Reference data that translates codes to labels within one system, such as state code to state name. A crosswalk instead bridges two different systems.
A view whose results are stored. It is faster to query than a plain view, but it must be refreshed to stay current.
Data about data, such as its type, source, owner, freshness, and meaning.
A change to an award or subaward after it was first funded.
The cost base most federal indirect rates apply to: direct costs minus certain excluded items. Check 2 CFR 200.1 for the current exclusions.
A budget requested in fixed blocks without detailed line items. Check the sponsor's guidance for current block sizes and limits.
A section of the UDM that covers one recognizable kind of work the institution does, such as "we have an IRB."

A problem found while monitoring an award, such as a high burn rate. It is recorded as an Action with the Monitoring_Exception type. A late report does not create one automatically. Late is the report's own status, and an exception is a problem someone chose to log.
An arrangement in which two or more PIs share authority and responsibility for leading a project, under a written leadership plan, common at NIH.
The back-and-forth with a sponsor or subrecipient over agreement terms before they are accepted.
An award for a project funded for the first time. Renewals and funding added to an existing award do not count.
Extending an award's end date without adding money.
A modification status: no approval was needed, and the modification is kept for the record.
A decision status: the sponsor received the proposal but removed it from consideration without reviewing it.
A deliverable status: the deliverable is due and work has not started.

terms.also: NOA, award letter, notice of grant award
terms.definition: The sponsor's official document announcing an award and its terms.

terms.also: Proposal and Award Policies and Procedures Guide
terms.definition: NSF's rulebook for proposals and awards.
An action status: the task has been created and not started.
One rule pulled out of a funding opportunity, such as page limits, eligibility, required documents, or review criteria.
A free, permanent ID number for an individual researcher that follows them across institutions.
Any group that takes part in research funding: sponsors, the institution's own departments and colleges, subrecipients, vendors, and committees.
A role an organization plays, such as sponsor, subrecipient, or vendor. One organization can play several.
An outside ID number an organization carries, such as its UEI or tax ID.
All current and pending resources that support a person's research, wherever based and whether or not they have monetary value, which sponsors require disclosed.
A required report not submitted by its due date.
The set of files and forms assembled to send to the sponsor. If the package changes, its sign-off no longer applies.
A payment stage: the money has moved between the parties. An unplanned refund can start here.
R&D funds an institution sends to a subrecipient to carry out part of the work. Payments to contractors or vendors for goods and services do not count.
An organization that holds an award or subaward and issues a subaward to another organization to carry out part of the program. Buying goods or services from a vendor does not make it one.

Money moving between the parties to an award or subaward, as the agreement's payment terms provide. This covers sponsor payments to the institution, institution payments to a subrecipient, and refunds. Ordinary expenses on the award, such as vendors, consultants, and salaries, are Transaction rows.
Whether the money is Incoming to the institution or Outgoing from it. Every payment row states this.
How the sponsor pays: reimbursement after costs are incurred, advance payment, cost reimbursement contract, fixed price, letter of credit draws, or payment on request.
A decision status: the sponsor has the proposal and has not decided. It does not imply an award.
The dates during which work may be done and costs may be charged.
Anyone involved in research administration: faculty, staff, students, postdocs, residents, fellows, outside collaborators, and contacts at sponsors or subrecipients.
Effort expressed in months: the effort percentage times the months in the appointment.
The institutional policy on who may serve as principal investigator. Sponsors have their own expectations, so this can differ from whom a sponsor would accept.
Proposals sent to a sponsor and still awaiting a final decision, as a forecast of future funding.
A documented, repeatable procedure for a recurring task, with its tools, steps, responsible roles, and acceptance criteria. Onboarding a new source system to the UDM is one example.
An exception the institution grants to a rule, such as letting someone serve as PI who would not normally qualify, or waiving cost share or indirect costs.
A correction made to an award or subaward after it has closed, such as an audit finding or a late charge.
A correction made to an award or subaward after it has been terminated, such as an audit finding or a late charge.
The institution's permission to start spending before an award is official.

Costs incurred before an award's start date, in anticipation of the award and needed to do the work on time. They are at the institution's own risk until the award is made, and the sponsor's rules decide whether the award can cover them. The institution's permission to incur them is a pre-award authorization.
The award a subaward's money comes from.
The original source of the money when funding passes through another organization first.
The person who leads the project and is responsible for its science and administration.
Written permission the sponsor must give before certain changes, such as moving money, extending dates, or changing the PI.
How urgently an office should handle an item: low, medium, high, or critical.
Money a project earns during the award, such as fees or sales. Depending on the award terms, it reduces the award total (deduction), adds to project funds (addition), or counts toward cost share.
The sponsor's contact for the science and goals of a program or award.

terms.also: Sponsored project, grant, award, project ID, longitudinal project
terms.definition: A word with at least three different meanings in research administration, so always ask which one is meant: (1) a long-running research effort that may span many proposals and awards, (2) a single funded award, or (3) an accounting object in the financial system that collects costs.
A formal request for funding sent to a sponsor.
The total value requested by proposals sent to sponsors in a period. Repeated attempts at the same proposal count once.
The thread linking a proposal to the earlier proposals and later awards it is part of, so a long-running project can be followed over years.
How a proposal relates to earlier ones: new, resubmission, renewal, continuation, revision (supplement request), or task order.
The number of proposals sent to sponsors in a period. Repeated attempts at the same proposal count once.
A subaward status: the subaward is planned in the proposal, and no prime award exists yet.

terms.also: IRB protocol, IACUC protocol, IBC registration, study
terms.definition: The standing approved plan for a line of research reviewed by a committee.
A departure from what the approved protocol says to do. Major deviations affect safety or data and need committee review.

Spending on research and development that is separately accounted for in the institution's current operating funds, as the HERD survey counts it. It includes sponsored research, institutionally funded research, committed cost sharing, recovered and unrecovered indirect costs, equipment bought from R&D accounts, and funds passed through to subrecipients. It leaves out public service, non-research training grants, and capital projects. Check the current questionnaire for the full rules.

terms.also: NICRA, negotiated indirect cost rate agreement
terms.definition: The agreement between the institution and the federal government that sets its indirect cost (and often fringe) rates.
A budget revision that moves money between categories without changing the total funding.

A submission status: the attempt was pulled back to be corrected and resent. The institution still wants the sponsor to consider the proposal. The package must be fixed and signed off again, and the decision returns to Unrequested.
A submission status: the sponsor's system acknowledged the attempt.
A payment stage: the payment has been matched to the ledger.
How many years records must be kept after an award ends.

terms.also: F&A recovery, indirect cost recovery, overhead recovery
terms.definition: Indirect costs reimbursed by external sponsors.
Money moving backward. An Outgoing payment on an award is a refund to the sponsor. An Incoming payment on a subaward is a refund from the subrecipient.
A termination is called off or overturned, and the award or subaward returns to Active.
An internal approval status: an approval step refused the proposal, and it goes no further.
A modification status: the sponsor refused the modification, or the institution did where the sponsor's approval isn't needed.
An award that gives an existing project a further period of funding won through a new competition. A continuation, by contrast, involves no new competition.
An award or subaward that has started or finished closing returns to Active and can spend again.
An early setup status: at-risk spending has been requested and is not yet authorized.
A modification status: the modification has been requested and is waiting on approval by the sponsor, or by the institution where the sponsor's approval isn't needed.
The standard federal format for interim and final progress reports on research grants and cooperative agreements.
Protecting research from misappropriation that harms national or economic security, from related research integrity violations, and from foreign government interference.
Required training in research ethics, covering topics such as authorship, data management, and misconduct.
An operating limit on a proposal, award, subaward, person, or piece of equipment.
A revised version of a proposal that was previously not funded.
An internal approval status: the proposal was sent back for changes and must be routed again. An approval step can return it, approved material can change, or a withdrawn proposal can be revised.
A deliverable status: the sponsor sent it back for changes.
A modification status: an approved modification was later withdrawn by the sponsor or invalidated by correction. It no longer counts in the award's totals and dates, and its budget rows are unwound.
The kind of review an approval gets, such as exempt, expedited, or full board for human research.
An early setup status: the request or authorization was withdrawn before conversion or expiry.
A low, medium, or high rating that sets how closely something is reviewed and monitored.
A sponsor limit on the salary rate that can be charged; the part above the cap must be paid from other money.
The federal website where organizations register to receive federal money and where UEIs are issued.
A payment stage: the payment is expected under the payment terms, and nothing has been billed yet.
The formal structure of a dataset: its tables, columns, data types, constraints, and relationships. It describes structure, not the values stored.
The process of deciding how one schema corresponds to another. Crosswalks record the decisions.
The gate that decides whether a specific package may be sent. It is tracked in sponsor submission.
A submission status: the authorized organizational representative signed off on the current package, with any release to submit. It is ready to send.
A yearly organization-wide audit of federal award spending, required of non-federal organizations above a spending threshold. Check 2 CFR 200.501 for the current threshold and who is covered.
Software you use over the internet and pay for by subscription, rather than installing and running it yourself.

Where R&D money originally came from, in the HERD survey's categories: U.S. federal government, state and local government, business, nonprofit organizations, institutional funds, and all other sources. Federal money passed through another institution counts as federal.
Conditions that apply to one award beyond the standard terms.
Spending means expenses, plus or minus any corrections to them such as cost transfers, adjustments, and reversals.
The organization that pays for the work.

Money spent from externally sponsored awards, including research and non-research awards, with direct costs and the indirect costs charged to them. Open purchase orders and the institution's cost share do not count, matching how expenditures are reported to sponsors. See Spending for what counts as money spent.
The person the sponsor recognizes as principal investigator on an award, under the sponsor's rules. This is often the same person as the internal PI, but not always.
A report owed to the sponsor, such as a progress, financial, final, invention, data-sharing, or equipment report.

terms.also: OSP, SPA, Office of Sponsored Projects, Sponsored Programs Administration
terms.definition: The institutional unit that handles the lifecycle of sponsored projects, from proposal review through closeout.

terms.also: Grant administrator, award administrator, assigned specialist
terms.definition: Which person in the research office is responsible for a given proposal, award, or subaward.
One part of the path with its own set of statuses. Internal approval, sponsor submission, and sponsor decision are on the Proposal record. Award is on the Award record.
What a person is registered or certified to do, independent of any specific proposal or award.
A named block of SQL kept in the database and run on request. It can perform several steps in sequence, and its syntax is specific to the database product.

terms.also: Subagreement, outgoing subaward, subcontract (when it carries out part of the award)
terms.definition: An agreement in which the institution passes part of its award's work and money to another organization.
A bill from a subrecipient for work done under a subaward.
One send of a proposal to a sponsor's system.
Where a proposal stands in submission: unapproved, unsubmitted, signed off, submitting, submitted, received, validated, invalid, accepted, failed, or recalled.
A deliverable status: it was sent to the sponsor.
A submission status: the attempt was sent.
A submission status: the attempt is being sent.
The unit that prepares and submits the proposal.
The organization that receives a subaward and carries out part of the work.
Ongoing oversight of a subrecipient's work, spending, and compliance.
An assessment of a subrecipient's risk before issuing or continuing a subaward.

terms.also: Hit rate, funding rate, win rate
terms.definition: The share of reviewed applications that are funded, following NIH's method. An application and its resubmissions in the same fiscal year count once. Applications withdrawn or not reviewed are left out.
Extra money added to an existing award for added or expanded work. Unlike incremental funding, it wasn't part of the planned total.
An award status: spending was stopped by the sponsor or the institution, and it may resume.
A subaward status: work was stopped by the institution or the sponsor, and it may resume.
The tools people use to get the work done day to day, such as proposal routing, forms, and task tools.

terms.also: SoI, analytics layer, reporting layer, BI
terms.definition: Where data is turned into reports, dashboards, and analysis.

terms.also: SoR, source of truth, authoritative system
terms.definition: The official place where a piece of information lives. When two reports disagree, the System of Record wins.
A person's role on a proposal and, once funded, on the award, with effort, dates, and credit share.
A plan controlling who can access export-controlled items or information on a project.
An award status: the award ended before its period of performance finished, and termination processing is complete.
A subaward status: the subaward ended before its period of performance finished.
An award status: the award is being ended early, and termination is being processed. The sponsor, the institution, or both may have started it. Spending stops.
Ending an award before its scheduled end date, by the sponsor or the institution.

Why an award or subaward was terminated: Noncompliance, Mutual_Agreement, Recipient_Request, Sponsor_Priorities, or, for a subaward, Prime_Terminated. Executive orders use Sponsor_Priorities. The value is cleared on reinstatement.
The rules of a funded agreement: payment, reporting, special conditions, property, publication, closeout, and records retention.
Who owns a piece of equipment: the institution, the sponsor, the vendor, shared, or not yet decided.
Direct costs plus indirect costs.
Being able to follow a value, decision, or artifact back to its origin and forward to what depends on it. Data lineage is the form this takes for data.

terms.also: Charge, expense, ledger entry, journal line
terms.definition: A single entry posted to an award or subaward.

How long a step takes, in calendar days from when it started to when it finished, such as routing a proposal, setting up an award, or executing a subaward. Calendar days match how federal rules state their time limits.
A submission status: waiting on start. The material is not approved, so nothing can be sent.
A common, institution-neutral description of research administration data, so universities and vendors describe the same things the same way.
The main federal rulebook for managing grants and cooperative agreements: allowable costs, indirect costs, subrecipient monitoring, closeout, and audits.
The ID SAM.gov assigns to organizations, used to identify those receiving federal awards and subawards.
The federal funds on an award not yet spent or obligated, as reported on the federal financial report.
The indirect costs sponsors did not reimburse on externally funded R&D: the negotiated rate times its base, minus what was recovered. Amounts above what the negotiated rate would give do not count.
A decision status: waiting on start. No sponsor outcome is recorded, and either no attempt has been accepted since the latest approval or the newest attempt was recalled.
An award's funding minus money spent. Money set aside for future expenses still counts as unspent. See Spending for what counts as money spent.
A submission status: the material is approved, and the current package has not been signed off or sent.
An action status: the task was attempted and did not achieve its outcome.
A submission status: the attempt passed the sponsor's system checks.
A saved query that behaves like a table. It stores no data of its own, and it returns current results each time it runs.
A status that holds a place until the earlier stage is finished.
A deliverable status: the sponsor no longer requires it.
A modification status: the request was withdrawn before a decision.

A decision status: a submitted proposal was pulled from the sponsor's consideration, and no decision is requested any longer. The institution then chooses one of two outcomes: stop here, and Withdrawn is the final status, or revise and try again, and internal approval returns to Returned and the decision to Unrequested.
A task attached to a record. It tells you what needs doing and who is doing it.
